instructions: Agent Hotline lets coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) phone and text their owner and turns the owner's spoken or texted answer into agent input, including permission approvals. A phone line that steers agents is a remote control for the developer's machine. Read AGENTS.md and docs/plan.md for invariants. Prioritize: anything that could approve without the owner's explicit words, unverified webhooks, non-owner callers getting information, secrets leaving the machine, agent-supplied text influencing decisions, loops that call repeatedly, and hook output that does not match the agent's documented format. Most PRs are written by autonomous agents: be specific, cite the line, and skip praise.

rules.rule: No answer, a failed call, a timeout, an error or an unclear reply must never produce an approval or a fabricated answer. Flag any default-allow path.

Calls and texts may only go to the configured owner number; inbound calls and texts from other numbers must be rejected without disclosing anything; inbound calls must check the PIN before reading status or accepting instructions.
Every public route must verify the Twilio signature or the ElevenLabs secret/HMAC before reading the body, and reject replays. Flag any public route without verification.

Text written by agents (questions, command previews, summaries) is untrusted. It must never be able to approve itself or change who is called. Flag code that derives a decision from agent-supplied text.

Anything sent to Twilio or ElevenLabs must pass through the redaction function; secrets, tokens, private keys and .env values must never leave the machine. Phone numbers in logs show the last four digits only.
Flag any change that loosens a test assertion, timeout, scenario, or makes scripts/ci/run.sh or the scenario runner succeed without exercising the system.
Tests and the scenario suite must not call real Twilio, ElevenLabs or any network service, or touch the real ~/.claude or ~/.codex.
